name: Central bank stress
value: Dec Fed rise 93% priced; yen near 159.4
summary: Futures price a 93% chance of a December Fed rise; yen near 159.4 per dollar as Tokyo keeps warning of intervention
state: Fed funds futures on 16 Nov implied a 93.4% chance of a quarter-point rise at the 9 Dec meeting and 6.6% for a half-point move, down from 11.5% on 13 Nov (Reuters). The yen traded near 159.4 per dollar on 16 Nov after data showed Japan's economy shrank an annualised 0.1% in July–September; Finance Minister Katayama warned on 13 Nov against one-sided moves (Yahoo Finance). Central banks face a stagflationary dilemma, but no emergency inter-meeting move or new intervention was found as of 16 Nov.
for_you: Borrowers on variable-rate loans and mortgages are exposed to further rate rises. Travellers and importers dealing in yen are exposed to sharp currency swings if Japan intervenes.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma and open G7 FX intervention threat (yen ~159); no emergency move (Alert)

sources.title: Reuters via SRN News — Dollar extends rally, yen looks past soft Japan GDP data
Yahoo Finance — Japanese yen tests 160 again, drawing intervention threats

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
